sentences: A woman in a yellow jeogori, the traditional Korean jacket, is shown from the waist up, her gaze turned slightly to the right.
The red collar and ties and the black cloth behind her make the yellow leap forward.
The paint is so thin that the weave of the canvas shows through, and a few quick, bold strokes are enough to catch her firmly closed lips and bright eyes.
Because he left out detail and used strong colour, Kim Jong-tae is often compared with the Fauves and the Expressionists.
In 1936 the painter-critic Kim Yong-jun wrote that the picture showed a clear wish to capture a flavour unique to Korea.
Kim, from Gimpo, worked as a primary school teacher and from 1926 won repeated prizes at the Joseon Art Exhibition.
He died suddenly of illness in 1935, still in his twenties, while holding a solo show in Pyongyang, and so few of his works survive that this one has come to stand for his art.
